name: Phi-3.5-vision-instruct
notes: TWO-PART MODEL. (1) Vision: openai/clip-vit-large-patch14-336 (img_processor.model_name, image_dim_out 1024), num_img_tokens 144. Per crop: (336/14)^2 = 576 patches pooled 2x2 -> 144 tokens, matching the declared num_img_tokens exactly. DYNAMIC CROPPING / HD TRANSFORM: use_hd_transform true, hd_transform_order 'sub_glb', with_learnable_separator true, projection_cls 'mlp', and preprocessor_config num_crops 4. HD transform emits the global 448-equivalent view plus up to 4 sub-crops of 336, separated by learned separator tokens. VISION TOKENS: 5 views * 144 = 720 tokens per image at the num_crops 4 default, plus separator tokens. DOMINANCE: VISION DOMINATES -- 720 vision tokens vs a ~100-token text prompt, ~7:1. Note this is 2x cheaper than Phi-4-multimodal at its default because num_crops 4 is far below dynamic_hd 36. (2) LLM: Phi-3.5 dense decoder, 32 layers, hidden 3072, 32 heads AND 32 KV heads (MHA, no GQA), head_dim 96 (3072/32, narrower than Phi-4's 128), intermediate 8192, vocab 32,064, max_position 131,072 vs original_max_position_embeddings 4096. ARCHITECTURE = dense. CONTEXT_SCALING = LongRoPE, rope_scaling.long_factor per-dimension array, rope_theta 1e4. KV CACHE: 32 * 32 * 96 * 2 * 2 = 393,216 B/token (384 KiB) -- TIED FOR THE LARGEST KV-PER-TOKEN IN THIS SLICE. The narrow head_dim 96 keeps it from being worse: a conventional MHA at Phi-3.5's width would be 512 KiB/token. Even so, at 131,072 ctx this is 48.0 GiB per sequence at bf16, so Phi-3.5-vision is a short-context model in practice despite the 131k headline. This is the clearest example in the slice of MHA being the wrong default in a modern VLM. params_b 4.147 = HF API safetensors total (4,146,621,440); the Phi-3.5-mini text model is ~3.8B.
